# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — 2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap

## 1. Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | Source of all malicious HTTP POSTs; source of SMB/Kerberos alert traffic to the DC |
| MAC | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==172.17.0.99`), matches `eth.src` on all frames from this IP |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP option 12 (hostname, tied to MAC `18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4`); confirmed via NBNS `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>/<20>`; also seen in DNS (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com`) |
| Domain / NetBIOS workgroup name | BEPOSITIVE (AD domain `bepositive.com`, DC `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19` at 172.17.0.17) | NBNS, DNS SRV records for `_ldap._tcp....bepositive.com` |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 172.17.0.99 and the DC (172.17.0.17) |

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer) — an information-stealer/loader family.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The commercial Suricata/ET rule `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` fired 48 times on POST traffic from 172.17.0.99 to 79.124.78.197 (alerts file, event #3.1504). This is corroborated behaviorally: repeated POSTs of the form `<len>|<GUID>|<random-token>|<base64-blob>` to `/foots.php` on that host, using a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer 7 User-Agent, at intervals of roughly 40–90 seconds for the remainder of the capture (~58 minutes) — classic stealer beaconing/checkin behavior.

A distinct earlier phase (t≈160s) shows a pay-per-install-style loader gate: an HTTP GET to `/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` with no User-Agent/browser fingerprint, returning a plaintext bot-ID line `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`, followed immediately by a POST to `/index.php` exchanging encrypted binary blobs. This is the delivery/registration stage that precedes the Koi Stealer checkin traffic and is consistent with a loader-as-a-service ("subid" affiliate/campaign tag) dropping the stealer.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### C2 endpoints
- **79.124.78.197:80** — Koi Stealer C2 (signature-confirmed via ETPRO rule). Bare-IP `Host:` header used for every request (no domain lookup precedes it — DNS query log shows no A-record request for this IP), a strong C2 tell.

### Bot/session identifiers observed in traffic (not classic domain/hash IOCs, but campaign-specific)
- Loader bot ID / subid: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U`
- Stealer bot GUID: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` (seen prefixing every `/foots.php` POST body)

### URLs
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — repeated stealer exfil/checkin POST (48 occurrences, confirmed by ETPRO signature)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — loader gate GET
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — loader gate POST (encrypted binary exchange, response payload)

### Suspicious secondary infrastructure
- **46.254.34.201** (TLS SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) — 701 KB downloaded over ~102 seconds beginning at t≈153s, immediately preceding the first Koi Stealer C2 checkin at t≈156s. Content is TLS-encrypted and cannot be inspected directly, but the timing (large download immediately before C2 activity starts) is consistent with this being the compromised/malicious delivery site for the initial payload. Flagged as suspicious, not signature-confirmed.

### Domain
No malicious domain was resolved via DNS for the C2 host — all `/foots.php` and `/index.php` traffic went directly to the bare IP 79.124.78.197. `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (resolved via TLS SNI to 46.254.34.201, no DNS query captured for it either) is the one non-Microsoft/non-infrastructure domain observed and is noted above as the probable delivery vector.

### Files / hashes
No cleartext executable (PE) was recoverable from HTTP objects in this capture — the loader exchange (`/index.php` POST/response) carries an encrypted binary blob, not a plain file, so no meaningful SHA256 of a malware binary can be computed from this traffic alone. HTTP objects extracted and hashed:
- `foots.php` (all 48 responses): SHA256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` — this is the hash of an **empty response body** (server ACKs the stealer POST with 0 content-length), not a payload.
- `index.php` response (t≈161s): SHA256 `ed0855c1637e5f93be7d54acb2cb8872683a0e5eb670258abb1ebc41bfbf459` — encrypted/opaque binary blob from the loader gate, not a decodable file.

## 4. Benign Context (excluded from IOCs)
- SMB/Kerberos/RPC alerts (`ET INFO SMBv1`, `GPL NETBIOS ... overflow`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow`) between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17 are standard, if noisy, legacy AD/SMBv1 domain-join and Kerberos authentication traffic — false-positive-prone signatures on normal enterprise traffic, not malicious.
- `www.msftconnecttest.com`, Windows Update (`ctldl.windowsupdate.com`), MSN/Bing/Office 365/Microsoft telemetry domains, `acroipm2.adobe.com` (Adobe update check `ProcessMAU.txt`), and `sso.godaddy.com` are all legitimate OS/application background traffic.

## Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on the BEPOSITIVE domain, was infected with **Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed via ETPRO rule). The infection chain begins with a large encrypted download from a suspicious host masquerading as an Italian confectionery site (46.254.34.201 / bellantonicioccolato.it), followed immediately by a pay-per-install-style loader gate check-in to 79.124.78.197 (`/index.php`, subid `qIOuKk7U`) that exchanges an encrypted payload, after which the host begins sustained Koi Stealer C2 beaconing to the same IP (`/foots.php`) roughly every 40–90 seconds for the remainder of the nearly one-hour capture, exfiltrating base64/encrypted data blobs tagged with bot GUID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`.
